question.text: What will be NVIDIA's forward guidance in its Q3 FY2027 earnings release? (Operating expenses (GAAP))
question.resolution_criteria:
This question will resolve as the midpoint of the guidance range for Q4 FY2027 as stated in NVIDIA’s “Outlook” section of its Q3 FY2027 earnings press release, expected to be published on [NVIDIA’s investor relations site](https://nvidianews.nvidia.com/) and the [SEC’s EDGAR system](https://www.sec.gov/) on November 17, 2026.

The unit value for revenues is billions of U.S. dollars, and it will be rounded to the nearest billion. GAAP gross margin will be rounded to the nearest tenth of a percent. GAAP operating expenses are in a unit value of billions of U.S. dollars and will be rounded to the nearest tenth of a billion dollars.
question.fine_print:
* If a single figure (not a range) is provided, that figure will be used.
* If multiple ranges or scenarios are presented, the primary range specified in the official “Outlook” or “Guidance” section will be used to resolve the subquestions.
* If NVIDIA does not issue guidance for Q4 FY2027 in the Q3 FY2027 release, the corresponding subquestion will be **annulled**.
* Only the originally published figure will be used; subsequent updates, corrections, or guidance revisions will be ignored.

research:
Nothing has settled this yet. NVIDIA hasn't published its Q3 FY2027 release or confirmed the report date. Kress's full-year opex comment implies Q4 GAAP opex of roughly $9.4-10.1B. Some estimates below are my own arithmetic, not NVIDIA figures.

## 1. Resolution source
- 2026-08-26: The Q2 FY2027 release (the latest source) guides Q3 GAAP opex to about $9.2B and non-GAAP to about $9.0B. Q2 FY27 actual GAAP opex was $8,408M; Q1 FY27 was $7,621M. [NVIDIA](https://nvidianews.nvidia.com/news/nvidia-announces-financial-results-for-second-quarter-fiscal-2027), [8-K on EDGAR](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001045810/000104581026000073/q2fy27pr.htm)
- The question resolves on the "approximately $X billion" GAAP opex figure for Q4 FY27 in the Q3 FY27 release. NVIDIA usually gives a single number, not a range.

## 2. Current status
- 2026-10-28: Nothing settles it yet. The Q3 FY27 release is not out.
- The report date is not confirmed, and the sources disagree:
  - The question says November 17.
  - Kalshi's earnings-call market says November 18.
  - Der Aktionär says November 19.
- A CME tracker (as of 2026-10-21) and a 2026-09-28 article both said no date had been announced. I found no official "Sets Conference Call" notice for Q3 FY27. Last year's notice came on 2025-10-29 for a 2025-11-19 report. [CME](https://www.cmelitegroup.com/knowledge-hub/nvidia-earnings-date/), [Trend and Ticker](https://trendandticker.com/markets/semiconductors/nvidia-earnings-date-q3-fiscal-2027-2026), [Der Aktionär](https://www.deraktionaer.de/artikel/deraktionaerplus/nvidia-erst-doener-dann-super-zahlen-20424952.html)

## 3. Recent news (newest first)
- 2026-10-27: Microsoft, Alphabet and Amazon report on October 28-29. Their capex is the key demand signal for NVIDIA. [Motley Fool](https://www.fool.com/investing/2026/10/27/big-tech-is-about-to-report-nvidia-investors-should-watch-one-number/)
- 2026-10-20: Musk said SpaceX plans to add 10 GW of AI compute in 2027, using only NVIDIA chips. [Motley Fool](https://www.fool.com/investing/2026/10/26/elon-musk-and-spacex-just-delivered-incredible-new/)
- 2026-08-26 (Q2 call): CFO Kress said "we now expect OPEX to grow in the low 50s" for FY27. She cited a broader product portfolio and more use of AI tools. Q2 GAAP opex rose 10% from Q1, mainly on compute infrastructure and compensation costs. [Transcript](https://transcripts.platformaeronaut.com/transcripts/NVDA-2Q27-transcript)
- 2026-05 (Q1 call): The full-year opex growth guide was "upper 40s" percent, so it was raised in August. [Summary](https://transcripts.platformaeronaut.com/summaries/NVDA-1Q27-AI-Summary)
- Starting with Q1 FY27, non-GAAP no longer excludes stock-based compensation, so GAAP and non-GAAP are now only about $0.2B apart.

## 4. Base rates: GAAP opex guidance vs. actuals
| Quarter | Guide (GAAP) | Actual | Guide minus prior-quarter actual |
|---|---|---|---|
| Q3 FY26 | ~$5.9B | $5.839B | +$0.49B |
| Q4 FY26 | ~$6.7B | $6.794B | +$0.86B |
| Q1 FY27 | ~$7.7B | $7.621B | +$0.91B |
| Q2 FY27 | ~$8.5B | $8.408B | +$0.88B |
| Q3 FY27 | ~$9.2B | due Nov | +$0.79B |

Sources: [Q3 FY26 PR](https://nvidianews.nvidia.com/news/nvidia-announces-financial-results-for-third-quarter-fiscal-2026), [Q4 FY26 PR](https://nvidianews.nvidia.com/news/nvidia-announces-financial-results-for-fourth-quarter-and-fiscal-2026), [Q1 FY27 PR](https://nvidianews.nvidia.com/news/nvidia-announces-financial-results-for-first-quarter-fiscal-2027)

- Actuals have usually landed within about ±$0.3B of guidance, mostly a little below. Q4 FY26 was the exception, coming in above.
- For the last four quarters, the new guide has been about $0.8-0.9B above the latest actual.
- Implied Q4 from the full-year guide (my own calculation; the Q1 FY26 figure is from memory and unverified):
  - FY26 GAAP opex is about $23.08B. That uses Q1 FY26 ≈ $5.03B plus the verified $5.413B, $5.839B and $6.794B.
  - Growth in the "low 50s" (50-53%) gives FY27 of about $34.6-35.3B.
  - Q1 + Q2 actuals + the Q3 guide total $25.23B, which leaves about $9.4-10.1B for Q4. The 51.5% midpoint gives about $9.7B.
  - The answer moves with Q3 actuals: if Q3 comes in under $9.2B, the implied Q4 rises.
  - If Kress's percentage refers to non-GAAP (now including SBC), the result is similar.
- Simple extrapolation: about $9.1-9.2B Q3 actual plus $0.8-0.9B gives about $9.9-10.1B.

## 5. Other forecasts
- I found no market or analyst consensus on NVIDIA's Q4 GAAP opex guidance.
- Related markets (fetched 2026-10-28):
  - Polymarket, Q3 non-GAAP gross margin: 73-75% at 84.5%.
  - Polymarket, Q3 Data Center revenue: above $100B at 80%; above $105B at 27.5%.
  - Kalshi, FY2027 headcount: above 50k at 81%; above 52k at 41%. Headcount drives compensation opex.
  - Kalshi's earnings-call mention market dates the call to November 18.
- None of these resolve on opex directly.

## 6. Upcoming events before resolution
- Expected around late October or early November: NVIDIA's notice confirming the call date.
- 2026-10-28/29: Microsoft, Alphabet and Amazon earnings, with capex commentary.
- November 17-19 (unconfirmed): the Q3 FY27 release and CFO commentary. Watch for Q3 actual opex and whether the full-year "low 50s" growth outlook changes.
- Possible upside to opex: acquisitions or deal-related costs (for example the Groq deal; Kalshi gives a DOJ fine 7%), and possible legal or accrual items, which only GAAP includes.

forecasts.reasoning:
(a) About 20 days remain. NVIDIA's Q3 FY2027 release is expected around November 17-19, 2026. The exact date is not yet confirmed.

(b) The latest value is from the August 26, 2026 release, which guided Q3 FY27 GAAP opex to about $9.2B. Recent actuals were $7.621B in Q1 FY27 and $8.408B in Q2 FY27.

(c) If nothing changed, the guide would stay flat at about $9.2B. That is unrealistic given NVIDIA's steady pattern of sequential opex growth.

(d) If the current trend continued, each new guide has come in about $0.8-0.9B above the latest actual. A Q3 actual of about $9.1-9.2B would give a Q4 guide of about $9.9-10.1B. The full-year "low 50s" opex growth comment points slightly lower, to about $9.4-10.1B with a midpoint near $9.7B. Two things could push it higher:
- The full-year growth outlook was raised last quarter, from "upper 40s" to "low 50s", and could be raised again.
- If the Q3 actual comes in under $9.2B, the implied Q4 figure rises.

(e) Historical variation: quarter-to-quarter guide increments have ranged from +$0.49B to +$0.91B, and actuals have landed within ±$0.3B of the guide. That puts the plausible spread for the Q4 guide at roughly ±$0.4B around the center.

(f) There is no direct consensus or market on this figure. The full-year guide arithmetic centers near $9.7-9.8B, and trend extrapolation centers near $10.0B. The question creator's range is $9.5-11.2B.

(g) Low scenario: NVIDIA reins in hiring or infrastructure spend, or the Q3 actual comes in high so the remaining full-year budget is small. The guide could then be about $9.3-9.4B. High scenario: a costly acquisition or integration (for example Groq-related costs), legal accruals, a big compute-infrastructure ramp, or another raise to the full-year growth outlook. Any of these could push the guide to $10.5B or more.
